html:
A Chinese chemist who discovered artemisinin, a drug against malaria that has saved millions of lives. In 2015 she won the Nobel Prize in medicine, the first citizen of the People's Republic of China to win a Nobel Prize in a science.

In 1969, during the Cultural Revolution, she was put in charge of a secret military project, Project 523, to find a malaria cure for North Vietnamese troops in the Vietnam War, who were dying from strains that resisted older drugs. Her team searched old Chinese medical texts and tested hundreds of herbal remedies. Sweet wormwood, qinghao, gave promising but uneven results. A text from the 4th century by the physician Ge Hong said to soak it in cold water. Tu guessed that heat was destroying the active part, and used a low temperature extraction, which worked.

Artemisinin based combination drugs became the standard malaria treatment worldwide from the 2000s. Tu had no doctorate and no foreign training, which made her prize a surprise in China.
